text:
priya: Quick heads-up — saw sustained memory growth on a Dedicated canary serving long-context LLMs (40k-80k tokens). Heap grows until OOM. Repro on canary-3 with steady traffic.

matt: Which component is allocating? KV pages or runtime buffers?

priya: pprof shows majority of growth attributed to kv_cache_pages (approx 68%) and small fragments piling up. Attached pprof snapshot: 
```
(pprof) top10
Showing nodes accounting for 72.34s, 98.7% of 73.33s total
      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
  12.34s 16.8% 16.8%   12.34s 16.8%  runtime.mallocgc
  50.12s 68.3% 85.1%   50.12s 68.3%  runtime.kv_cache_pages.alloc
```

anya: Hmm. Any recent changes to cache key derivation or session tagging?

sam: I ran git-bisect, regression lands in commit abcdef1 (kernel+batching refactor). That commit changed cache key to include `session_id` for more accurate per-session eviction.

priya: Yep — we now include `session_id` inside `kv_key`. Old key: `prefix|model|tenant`. New key: `prefix|model|tenant|session_id`.
```
// old
func kvKey(prefix, model, tenant string) string {
  return prefix + "|" + model + "|" + tenant
}
// new (intro'd in abcdef1)
func kvKey(prefix, model, tenant, sessionID string) string {
  return prefix + "|" + model + "|" + tenant + "|" + sessionID
}
```

matt: That would massively reduce reuse across requests. With long contexts, every session creates its own pages and fragments, leading to fragmentation + no cross-request hits.

priya: Exactly. The canary workload has many long-lived sessions that were previously sharing prefix caches. With session_id in key those become separate cold allocations. Memory ramps.

sre-oncall: Can we mitigate immediately without a full revert? Low-risk hotfix options?

anya: Ideas: 1) strip session_id from key for prefixes only (keep for per-session metadata buckets), 2) add an LRU compaction pass that coalesces small fragments into contiguous pages, 3) introduce a TTL smoothing policy so newly-created keys start with short TTL then grow if reused.

sam: I tried a patch locally that canonicalizes prefix keys (reverts session_id inclusion for keys that match prefixPattern). Quick numbers:
before patch (canary-3, 1h): RSS ~ 42GB, kv_pages ~ 28GB
after patch (canary-3, 1h): RSS ~ 18GB, kv_pages ~ 9GB
No functional regressions on tests.

matt: Nice. Can you push an RFC PR with the change + a regression test that simulates concurrent long-context sessions and measures reuse ratio? We should measure hit-rate and fragmentation metrics:
- prefix_reuse_ratio
- avg_fragment_size
- page_fill_factor

priya: On it. Also adding a perf hook to emit per-tenant prefix hit histogram to console for 1h after deploy so we can detect churn spikes.

infra-bot: deploy request queued for canary-rollback-hotfix by sam. CI: 2/3 (flake in runtime-tests).

anya: Another note — kernel selection changes in abcdef1 also increased batch size for longctx paths, which inflates KV prefetch windows and forces more pages into memory per request. We should tune `max_prefetch_pages_per_request` down for longctx path until reuse stabilizes.

priya: Good catch. I'll add a runtime flag to cap prefetch when session_length > 16k. Quick heuristic: max_prefetch = min(16, int(session_len/1024)).

sre-oncall: For monitoring, add alert if kv_pages_delta > 5GB over 10m on a node. That'll catch runaway cases pre-OOM.

sam: Proposed follow-ups:
- short-term: merge prefix-canonicalization hotfix + prefetch cap to canary cluster, run 6h soak
- medium: implement compaction pass that runs during low-qps windows to defragment kv slab (goal: reclaim ~30% of small fragments)
- long-term: redesign keying to a two-level scheme: canonical prefix -> per-session overlay (overlay stored as weak map with soft references)

priya: I'll open the PRs. Tests in `eng-runtime/kv` will include a microbenchmark that spins up 200 sessions with 50k tokens to measure steady-state RSS.

matt: For the perf regression writeup, include: pprof snapshots, bisect commit, before/after RSS + kv_pages, and flamegraphs for allocation paths. Keep it short for eng-review.

anya: Also add a short note for product: customers hitting long-context might see cost bump if keys stay session-scoped. We should surface recommended config for Dedicated customers now.

priya: Agreed. PRs shortly. Will DM bench logs to anyone who wants them. :mag: 

infra-bot: deploy canary-hotfix applied to canary-3 (rev: def4567) — monitoring enabled.

sam: Early signal (30m): kv_pages down 55%, prefix_reuse_ratio up from 18% -> 62%. No errors.

matt: Excellent. Follow-up: schedule compaction work for next sprint and add a small e2e that asserts prefix_reuse_ratio > 50% on longctx workload.

priya: Filing JIRA: RINF-1298 (kv-prefetch-compaction) and RINF-1299 (prefix-reuse-e2e).
